extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying for SSHRC Insight Grants (established and early-stage applicants in the social sciences and humanities)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation criteria and procedural guidance for SSHRC Insight and Insight Development Grant applications, describing how merit review committees score Challenge, Feasibility, and Capability and what applicants can expect in feedback and EDI consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge — The aim and importance of the endeavour (50%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenge — The aim and importance of the endeavour (50%)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points considered: Originality, significance, and expected contribution to knowledge; Appropriateness of the literature review; Appropriateness of the theoretical approach or framework; Appropriateness of the methods/approach; Quality of the training and mentoring to be provided to students, emerging scholars and other highly qualified personnel; Potential for the project results to have influence and impact within and/or beyond the social sciences and humanities research community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility — The plan to achieve excellence (20%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Feasibility — The plan to achieve excellence (20%)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points considered: Appropriateness of the proposed timeline, plan and probability of completion; Appropriateness of the requested budget and justification of proposed costs; Quality of, and commitment to, training to be provided; Strategy for ensuring outputs and other results are available to interested users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capability — The expertise to succeed (30%)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points considered: Quality, quantity, and significance of past experience and published and/or creative outputs; Relevant experience and training of any team members and collaborators; Potential to make important contributions; Quality of past contributions to the training of students, emerging scholars and other highly qualified personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring and thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: How merit review committee members score applications and how final scores are calculated and applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merit review committee members assign a score for each of the three criteria; appropriate weighting (Challenge 50%, Capability 30%, Feasibility 20%) is applied to arrive at a final score. Applications must receive a score of 3.0 or higher for each of the three criteria to be recommended for funding. Score scale: typically 1 (poor) to 6 (excellent), with intermediate scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process (competitive merit review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural standard describing how applications are evaluated and how funding decisions are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are reviewed through a competitive merit review process; a merit review committee makes recommendations; SSHRC bases funding decisions on committee recommendations and available funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback to applicants
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All applicants receive SSHRC's notice of decision, any external assessments received, and a summary of the merit review committee's evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: EDI-related factors that are taken into account during peer review (not explicitly scored as separate criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered factors include equity, diversity, and inclusion in research design; access considerations; indigenization; decolonization; and intersectionality. Note: these are considered during peer review but are not listed as separate scored criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application categories and funding ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: Program category guidance and typical funding envelopes for applicants to choose the appropriate competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insight Grants: $7K–$400K over 2–5 years — intended for established researchers. Insight Development Grants: $7K–$75K over 1–2 years — intended for exploratory/early-stage research. (This guides applicants on the appropriate program and scale of project.)
